title: Reverse Disjoint Intervals in Linked List
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list of length `n` and a 2D integer array `intervals`, where each `intervals[i] = [l, r]` (`1 <= l <= r <= n`) specifies a 1-indexed inclusive range of positions, all intervals in `intervals` are guaranteed to be **pairwise disjoint** (they may be given in any order, and two intervals may be directly adjacent such as `[1, 2]` and `[3, 4]`).

Reverse the nodes within every interval `[l, r]` in-place and return the head of the modified linked list. Aim for `O(n + m log m)` time where `m = intervals.length`.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
For every interval [l, r], 1 <= l <= r <= n, and all intervals are pairwise disjoint.
hints: Sort `intervals` by their starting index `l` so that every interval can be processed in a single left-to-right sweep over the linked list.

Maintain `prev` at 1-based index `pos`: for each `[l, r]`, advance `prev` until `pos == l - 1`, reverse the `r - l + 1` nodes starting at `prev.next`, and then set `prev` to the reversed segment's tail and `pos = r`.

examples.explanation: Sorting gives [1, 3] and [5, 7]; reversing positions 1..3 and 5..7 turns [1..7] into [3, 2, 1, 4, 7, 6, 5].
No intervals to reverse leaves [1, 2, 3] unchanged.
